Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

z3r 0.1.0

First release. z3r targets Z3 5.4.1 and builds against every Z3 release from 4.8.13; CI runs the tests on one release from each series on every push and on all 43 releases monthly. Features that need a newer Z3 than the one z3r was built with say which version they need.

Native foundation

  • Contexts created with Z3_mk_context_rc; every Z3 object is reference counted and keeps its context alive, so objects can be garbage collected in any order. Context configuration (z3_context(proof = TRUE, ...)) is validated.
  • Z3 errors become R errors without leaking references. Objects restored from saved sessions fail with a clear message instead of crashing. Objects from different contexts are rejected; z3_translate() copies between contexts.
  • configure locates Z3 through PKG_CPPFLAGS/PKG_LIBS, Z3_INCLUDE_DIR/Z3_LIB_DIR, pkg-config or common prefixes, links it by full path (on Linux with a run-time path that LD_LIBRARY_PATH cannot override), and refuses mismatched headers and libraries. configure.win supports official Windows release archives through Z3_DIR and installs their DLLs and license beside z3r. z3r refuses to load with a Z3 library other than the release it was compiled against.
  • Ctrl-C interrupts a running check.
  • z3_trace() switches Z3’s debug traces; z3_context() can enable concurrent reference count decrements.

Expressions

  • Int, Real, Bool, bit-vector, floating point, rounding mode, String, sequence, regular expression, character, array, set, datatype, finite domain and uninterpreted sorts, plus the complex, finite field and finite set sorts of Z3 5, with complex arithmetic and R complex literals.
  • Exact numerals from strings, R numbers and gmp numbers, with a documented conversion policy for doubles. z3_value() converts results to R without loss of precision.
  • R operators with z3r’s own sort checking.
  • Inspection (z3_kind(), z3_decl(), z3_args(), z3_decl_info(), z3_quantifier_info()), substitution, simplification with parameters, identifiers and print modes.
  • Strings with SMT-LIB escapes or from raw bytes, and their escaped and byte forms (z3_string_escaped(), z3_string_bytes()); rationals from a numerator and denominator; integer constant names; z3_sort_name().
  • Quantifiers and lambdas over de Bruijn indexed variables (z3_quantifier_db()) and printable patterns (z3_pattern()).
  • z3_ast_map(), a dictionary keyed by Z3 terms, and z3_format_terms().

Solving

  • Solvers with assertions, tracked assertions, assumptions, push/pop/reset, z3_with_scope(), model enumeration (z3_all_models()), models with staleness protection, hand-built models, unsatisfiable cores, proofs, consequences, cubes, units and trails, congruence classes, solving for variables, initial values, typed parameters, statistics (also as Z3’s text, z3_statistics_text()) and DIMACS export.
  • Timeouts for a single check (z3_check(timeout = )), which keep the other parameters of a solver or optimizer and restore the context’s timeout (also a global one in force when the context was made), and z3_interrupt(), which stops a solver’s or optimizer’s check from inside its own callbacks.
  • Optimization with hard and soft constraints, objectives (including the cost of soft constraint groups) and priorities, unbounded and non-attained optima, model callbacks, and, when a check returns "unknown", the bounds and the value of the best model found so far.
  • User propagators, clause callbacks and the proof checker callback. R errors and interrupts are raised safely after the check, callbacks cannot reenter their own solver, and callback closures do not keep their solver or context alive.

Theories and engines

  • Arithmetic, bit-vectors with overflow predicates, IEEE floating point, arrays (multi-index, map, default, lambdas), sets, strings, sequences, regular expressions and characters.
  • Algebraic datatypes: recursive, mutually recursive, enumerations, tuples (z3_tuple_fields()), lists and polymorphic datatypes.
  • Floating point formats by name or width (z3_fp_sort(ctx, "half")), SMT-LIB rounding mode names, and numeric parts of numerals.
  • Function interpretations with defaults set after creation (z3_model_set_default()); Datalog relation sorts (z3_relation_columns()).
  • Uninterpreted and recursive functions (recursive definitions need Z3 4.8.16), quantifiers with patterns and weights, special relations, pseudo-Boolean constraints.
  • Tactics, probes, goals and simplifiers.
  • The fixedpoint engine for constrained Horn clauses (Spacer) and Datalog, Spacer lemma callbacks (z3_on_lemma()), external Datalog relations (z3_fixedpoint_external()), and Spacer’s model-based projection (z3_model_project()), model extrapolation and z3_qe_lite().
  • Real closed fields, algebraic number arithmetic and polynomial subresultants.
  • SMT-LIB2 export, parsing and the SMT-LIB2 command interpreter.
  • Translation to and from the symcompR computer algebra package.
